title: Data Diodes: One-Way by Physics
description: An optical data diode enforces one-way data transfer in hardware: a transmitter LED on the low side, a receiver photodiode on the high side, and physically no return path — not a firewall rule, but the absence of a wire. Owl Cyber Defense and Waterfall Security build them for industrial and defense networks. What cannot physically return cannot leak.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Why One-Way: The Air-Gap Problem
description: Air-gapped networks still need data in — patches, threat intel, historian feeds — and every inbound path is a potential outbound leak. Data diodes solve the dilemma: information flows in, nothing flows out, by construction. Monitoring without exfiltration is the use case.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Optical Separation: The Core Mechanism
description: The diode's core is optical separation: electrical-to-optical conversion on the sending side, optical-to-electrical on the receiving side, with an air gap or fiber between. There is no electrical continuity to exploit and no reverse channel to sneak data through. Tampering with the optics breaks the link visibly.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Protocol Proxies and Breaks
description: TCP needs acknowledgments — which cannot cross a diode — so diode systems proxy protocols: they terminate TCP on each side and forward payloads across the optical link via UDP-style unidirectional protocols. File transfer, syslog, historian replication, and email all have diode-friendly proxies. The protocol break is the engineering that makes one-way usable.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Throughput and Performance
description: Modern diodes move serious traffic — gigabit-class throughput with low latency — because the optical link is just fast. Performance engineering covers packet pacing, forward error correction, and reassembly on the receiving side. One-way does not mean slow.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: EAL and Common Criteria Certification
description: High-assurance diodes pursue Common Criteria EAL certification (EAL4+, EAL7 for the strictest) proving the one-way property under evaluation. NERC CIP recognizes diodes for electronic security perimeters in the power grid. Certification turns a claim into evaluated fact.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Deployments: ICS and Power Grid
description: Data diodes guard industrial control systems: historian data flows out of the plant to the business network while control stays unreachable from it. Power grid operators deploy diodes at security perimeters. The plant talks; the plant cannot be talked to.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Diodes vs Firewalls
description: A firewall is software policy that can be misconfigured or exploited; a diode is physics that cannot be reconfigured into two-way. Defense in depth uses both: diodes where the direction must be absolute, firewalls where policy suffices. Do not substitute one for the other.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: File Transfer Across the Diode
description: Diode file transfer chops files into sequenced, checksummed chunks, blasts them across, and reassembles on receipt — with no acknowledgments, redundancy and FEC replace retransmission. Large files cross reliably one-way every day. The protocol does the reliability TCP cannot.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Monitoring and SIEM Feeds
description: Security monitoring crosses diodes outward: IDS alerts, logs, and SIEM feeds flow from the protected enclave to analysts without giving analysts' network a path back in. The SOC sees everything and touches nothing. Visibility without vulnerability.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Video and Streaming Across
description: Even video crosses diodes: unidirectional streaming protocols carry camera feeds out of secure areas to monitoring stations. Latency stays low enough for live watch. Seeing out without a path in is the point of the camera.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Testing the One-Way Property
description: The one-way property is tested adversarially: evaluators try to exfiltrate from the high side through every interface, timing channel, and fault they can devise. Passing means no path found under evaluation. This is security testing at its most literal.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Redundancy and High Availability
description: Critical diode deployments run redundant pairs with failover so the one-way path survives hardware failure. Monitoring watches link health, not just traffic. Availability engineering applies to physics too.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Covert Channels and Residual Risk
description: Honest diode engineering names residual risks: timing channels, compromised endpoints, and physical access are outside the diode's guarantee. The diode solves direction; the rest of the security program solves everything else. No single device is the whole program.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The One-Way Architecture
description: Ladder-top diodes: physics-enforced direction, proxied protocols, certified one-way property, deployed at perimeters, tested adversarially. Fifteen rungs from an LED and a photodiode to industrial networks that can report out but never be reached in.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.
